S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, and provide a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a material safety risk or requires inspection, mitigation, or product action.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The failure rate must not exceed 5% for any model, except where the regulator grants a time-limited, model-specific variance after reviewing independent test results and a documented corrective-action plan. Manufacturers must provide the per-model test results, including the failure rate, to customers considering or purchasing that model; results may not be withheld from those customers as confidential.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery models placed on the market 12 months or more after adoption must support remote emergency shut-off. For installed units, manufacturers must provide a remote-shutoff retrofit or equivalent compliant upgrade within 6 years after adoption, where technically feasible; any units not upgraded must be identified to their customers and the regulator with interim risk-mitigation instructions.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting the applicable performance requirements.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Customers must receive clear safety notices promptly when a known incident or test result indicates a material risk or requires inspection, mitigation, or product action. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop distribution of the affected model pending regulatory direction, and carry out the regulator-approved recall or corrective action.

document.section_notes: The final rules set a 24-hour regulator reporting deadline and a mandatory 8-per-100,000 recall trigger, but S2 now allows a renewable, model-specific variance above 5% with no fixed end, and S5 lets regulator-approved corrective action replace recall without a time bound. Northwind's red lines were met through a 6-year retrofit window and no public publication of per-model failure rates, while Halcyon's were met through per-model results going to customers and a 36-month suppression deadline.
